contentHtml:
New Delhi: The government has approved 19,983 health infrastructure units, including 2,151 Block Public Health Units, 744 Integrated Public Health Laboratories and 631 Critical Care Blocks, under the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), a senior health ministry official said on Thursday.Addressing a national-level orientation workshop on the National Health Mission (NHM) and PM-ABHIM in Bengaluru, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava stressed the need to strengthen public health infrastructure, disease surveillance and emergency preparedness through coordinated efforts between the Centre and states.

Advt

On the first day of the workshop, Srivastava emphasised the need for a mission-mode approach to accelerate progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), supported by robust situational awareness and effective inter-departmental coordination.She also highlighted the importance of leveraging digital health initiatives, particularly by strengthening linkages with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and Aarogya Setu, to facilitate integrated and efficient healthcare delivery.

On the second day, Srivastava underlined the need to strengthen the country's public health infrastructure, drawing on the experiences and lessons of the Covid pandemic.

Recalling the need for rapid augmentation of healthcare facilities, research capabilities, genomic sequencing and vaccine development during the pandemic, she said PM-ABHIM was conceived to enhance the country's preparedness to effectively respond to future pandemics and disease outbreaks.

She observed that while NHM contributes towards achieving key health-related SDGs through improved healthcare delivery, PM-ABHIM complements these efforts by strengthening the infrastructure, institutional capacities and systems required for public health resilience, emergency preparedness and pandemic response.

Advt

Srivastava also highlighted that the government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has accorded emphasis to greater capital investment in the health sector and the promotion of public-private partnerships to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and service delivery.

Launched on October 25, 2021, with a financial outlay of Rs 64,180 crore, PM-ABHIM aims to strengthen public health infrastructure, enhance disease surveillance and outbreak response capabilities, promote pandemic-related research and improve emergency preparedness and biosecurity.The mission has approved 19,983 infrastructure units across the country, marking significant progress in the expansion of healthcare facilities, diagnostic capabilities and critical care infrastructure.

Advt

Under the mission, grassroots healthcare infrastructure is being strengthened through the establishment of 11,001 Ayushman Arogya Mandir-Sub Health Centres at previously building-less locations and 5,456 Urban Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.The Free Drugs and Diagnostics Initiative further supports the availability of essential medicines and diagnostic services at these facilities, contributing to improved access to primary healthcare.The diagnostic and disease surveillance network has also been strengthened through 2,151 Block Public Health Units and 744 district-level Integrated Public Health Laboratories.

In addition, 631 Critical Care Blocks and 48 Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories have been supported under the Mission, enhancing capacities for timely diagnosis, disease management, critical care and research.Highlighting the central sector interventions under PM-ABHIM, Srivastava referred to the establishment of branches of the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) in different parts of the country to strengthen disease surveillance, outbreak investigation and response.Other important interventions include the development of quarantine facilities at major airports, strengthening of points of entry at airports and ports, and the establishment of metropolitan surveillance units in 20 cities.
